title: Spend exports and alert routing ideation
content:
Context and problem statement:

We need a more flexible, predictable spend export and alert-routing experience for customers who are trying to tie Redwood invoices / usage to their internal cost centers. Current pain points (from CS tickets and SE calls):
- Customers want exports that are immediately usable (not heavy post-processing). Right now exports sometimes require joining on multiple files to reconstruct allocation.
- Alerts are noisy or routed to the wrong teams. Example: infra team gets quota alerts for product features; finance wants high-level invoice sends only.
- Need to support both per-token micro-billing use cases (PLG apps) and enterprise reserved capacity models (monthly committed capacity) in the same export schema.

Goals for this doc:
- Propose UX patterns and data shapes for a single export surface that covers invoices, allocations, and budgets/alerts routing.
- Sketch wireframe copy and interactions for an "Export & Alerts" modal and a lightweight rule-builder for alert routing.
- Capture backlog items, edge cases, and acceptance criteria to hand to PM/ENG.

High-level product ideas (short):
1) Allocation Matrix: canonical mapping table that flattens invoice rows into "charge rows" with explicit dimension columns (customer_id, team_id, cost_center, sku, model, region, usage_type, start,end, quantity, unit_price, subtotal, allocation_share). Always export this as primary CSV/Parquet.
2) Export Presets: users can save/export presets that bake in date range, aggregation (daily/weekly/monthly), chosen dimensions, and anonymization options (hash user ids). Presets are shareable links.
3) Incremental Export API: support resume-able exports using cursor or file cursor id (so large accounts can incremental-sync).
4) Alert Routing Rules: visual rule builder that routes alerts (budget threshold, invoice generated, anomalous spend) to targets (email addresses, Slack channels, PagerDuty service, webhook). Rules can be scoped by team/cost_center/model.
5) Preview + Validation: before export/run, show sample 50 rows and highlight fields that will be present/omitted. For alert rules show example payload.

Wireframe writeups (modal + pages):
A) Export modal (primary flow)
- Trigger: Console header > Billing > Exports > New export
- Step 1: Scope
  - Quick selectors: date range, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), invoice vs usage vs both, preset dropdown
  - Advanced toggle: select dimensions to include (model, region, cost_center, label tag, rate_plan).
- Step 2: Format & destination
  - Format picker: CSV | Parquet | JSONL (newline delimited)
  - Compression: gzip | none
  - Destination: download | S3 bucket (pre-authorized) | GCS | Azure | SFTP | webhook (POST)
  - Incremental checkbox + window size (e.g., 1h, 6h, 24h) if destination supports resume
- Step 3: Transform rules (optional)
  - Map columns: cost_center = allocation_matrix.lookup(team_label)
  - Derived columns: "unit_cost_after_discount", "commit_surcharge"
  - PII masking: hash(user_id) | drop IPs
- Step 4: Preview & run
  - Show 50-row preview, sample schema, estimated file size, estimated tokens exported
  - Run now / schedule (cron-like UI) / save preset

Notes on Export UX micro-decisions:
- Use Parquet as default for large enterprise accounts; present CSV for small quick downloads.
- When destination is S3/GCS we should validate write credentials in a background job and fail fast.
- If incremental export selected, show required state id (cursor). Store in account metadata for resume.
- For multi-tenant exports (Dedicated) include a column "billing_scope" to indicate what portion of the invoice this row maps to (useful for chargebacks).

B) Alert routing rule-builder (page)
- Top: rule list with toggles (enabled/disabled), last triggered timestamp, matched scope badge (e.g., cost_center:payments-service)
- Create new rule modal: three columns
  1) WHEN (conditions): budget % thresholds (70/85/100), invoice generated, daily spend delta > X%, model cost > $Y, anomaly detection (optional ML toggle)
  2) SCOPE (selector): account-wide | product | team | cost_center | label-based selector | resource tag
  3) THEN (actions): send email list | Slack channel | PagerDuty | webhook | create ticket in Jira (project/prefix)
- Rule preview: JSON payload sample and estimated recipients (from directory lookup)
- Test button: run sample event through rule to show who would be notified (use masked data in UI)

Backlog items and grooming estimates (rough):
- B1: Allocation Matrix canonical schema + mapping engine (3 sprints)
- B2: Export modal basic (CSV download + preview) (2 sprints)
- B3: Destination integrations (S3, GCS, SFTP) (2-4 sprints depending on infra)
- B4: Incremental export backend and cursor mechanics (3 sprints)
- B5: Alert rule-builder frontend + delivery integrations (Slack/PagerDuty/webhook) (3 sprints)
- B6: Preview/validation & sampling endpoints (1 sprint)
- B7: QA: large account performance test & security review for PII masking (1 sprint)
- B8: Docs + SDK helpers for programmatic exports (1 sprint)
Estimated total: 13-17 sprints, can be parallelized across two teams (exports + alerts).

Edge cases & constraints:
- Reconciliation: exports must point back to invoice_id and line_item_id to make audits easy for finance. No transformations should break that traceability by default.
- Multi-currency: include currency columns and normalized USD column (include exchange_rate and as_of_date).
- Reserved capacity: we need to include committed vs overage breakdown so finance can map credits/commits.
- Attribution ambiguity: when usage is split across multiple cost centers (shared services), allow a fraction column (allocation_share) and a provenance column that references allocation rule id.
- GDPR/PII: default to conservative masking for user identifiers; provide admin opt-in for full IDs with audit logs and RBAC gate.
- Large exports timeout: run as background job with job id; provide websocket/long-poll progress updates in Console and link to stored file for 30 days.

Open questions (for PM sync):
- Should Parquet be first-class in the UI or behind an "enterprise feature" flag? (Impacts infra and QA)
- Export scheduling cadence minimum: minute-level? hourly? daily? Typical ask from customers is hourly and daily.
- Who owns S3 credential rotation and security review (platform infra or infra-integrations team)?
- Should we build templated mappings for common ERP/GL systems (NetSuite, Sage) as part of V1?

Acceptance criteria (example for B2 - Export modal basic):
- User can open modal, pick date range, choose CSV, preview 50 rows, and download file within 30s for medium-sized account (<= 100k rows).
- Export rows include invoice_id and line_item_id columns by default.
- Preview shows estimated file size and row count.
- Preset can be saved and appears in the preset dropdown for other users in the org.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Jordan: refine canonical allocation schema and create JSON schema draft (due 2026-03-10)
- Maya: mock up high-fidelity modal and rule-builder screens (Figma links) (due 2026-03-03)
- Sven: talk to infra about incremental export storage and cursor storage (sync by 2026-02-28)
- Priya: pull top 10 customer export ask logs and compile a short CSV of fields they need (due 2026-03-06)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough — focus feedback on the allocation matrix schema and the minimal required columns for auditability. Trying to avoid an export that’s "too transformed" for finance teams.

Quick sketch of proposed Allocation Matrix columns (order matters for many finance teams):
invoice_id, line_item_id, billed_customer_id, billed_org_name, billing_scope, period_start, period_end, usage_date, sku, model, region, resource_id, team_label, cost_center, allocation_rule_id, allocation_share, quantity, unit, unit_price, subtotal, currency, normalized_usd, tax, discount, commit_credit_applied, net_due, tags

End.
